title: Playing from the wrong teeing area
question: If you play your ball from the wrong teeing area, what is the correct ruling?

choices.text: You can continue playing your ball with no penalty if the shot was good.
You must cancel your shot and play again from the correct teeing area, with a penalty.
You must retake the shot without any penalty.
You receive a reward for being original.

explanation: If you play from the wrong teeing area, your shot does not count. In stroke play, you must cancel the shot, play from the correct teeing area, and add a two-stroke penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What happens if you hit your ball from the wrong tee box?
juniorVersion.question: If you start your shot from the wrong tee box (not the right place to start), what should you do?

choices.text: You can keep playing your ball with no penalty if your shot was good.
You must stop, ignore your last shot, and hit again from the right tee box, but you have to add extra shots to your score.
You can hit your shot again from the right spot without any extra shots given to you.
You get a prize for being different.

juniorVersion.explanation: If you hit from the wrong tee box, your shot doesn't count. You have to hit again from the correct place and add two extra shots to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The special area where you start each hole in golf.
Extra shots added to your score because of a mistake.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children where the correct tee box is by using tee markers and let them practise checking their position before hitting.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think the shot counts if it was a good one.
Kids may think there is no penalty or that they get a prize for starting from the wrong spot.
